# Read-Back

A sandwich ELISA assay is being performed on two 96-well plates to measure a secreted cytokine, with the two plates deliberately staggered 30 minutes apart. The coating step happens on Day 1 (overnight at 4 °C), and the assay itself runs on Day 2, spanning multiple incubation and wash cycles. The bottleneck is a single automated plate washer that can only process one plate at a time; every incubation step (blocking, antibody binding, substrate development) is bracketed by a wash on this washer. There is also one 37 °C incubator that can hold both plates simultaneously, one plate reader, and one operator. The protocol includes two upstream reagent prep steps (standard curve and sample dilutions) that must be ready before the assay steps that depend on them. There is no explicit deadline given; the work should finish as early as the constraints allow. The protocol is fully specified in the source text with no apparent gaps.
